#### Lemma. Stratifications versus connections with overconvergent Taylor series

*Node* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal-connection-form`.

For a frame (X, Y, P), the functor (E, ε) ↦ (E|_V, ∇) is an equivalence between overconvergent isocrystals in the stratification form (RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal) and locally free modules with integrable connection on strict neighbourhoods V of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P whose formal Taylor isomorphism ε(1 ⊗ m) = Σ_q (1/q!) ∇(D)^q(m) ⊗ τ^q (τ_i = 1 ⊗ t_i − t_i ⊗ 1 for local coordinates t_i on P near X) is induced by an analytic isomorphism p_2^*M ≅ p_1^*M on a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_{P²} in ]Y[_{P²}.

*Hypotheses.* P smooth near X with local coordinates t_1..t_n; the diagonal P → P × P is then a closed immersion with ]X[_P → ]X[_{P²} a fibration in open unit polydiscs (RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem).

*Proof outline.*

1. ε ↦ ∇: restrict ε to the first-order infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal (Berthelot 4.1).
2. ∇ ↦ ε: the Taylor series defines ε on the formal completion of the diagonal; the convergence hypothesis says it is induced by an analytic isomorphism on a strict neighbourhood; the cocycle condition holds formally, hence analytically since the tube of the diagonal is a polydisc fibration over ]X[ (RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem) and analytic functions on open polydiscs are determined by their Taylor expansion along the centre section (Berthelot 4.1, 4.2.1).

*Acceptance.*

- Dwork: ∇(1) = π dt gives Σ_q (1/q!) π^q (t' − t)^q = exp π(t' − t) (Berthelot 4.2.3).

*Uses.* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`.

*Sources.*

- Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique p, (4.2.1), p. 27: “Il revient au même de se donner un module à connexion intégrable (M,∇) sur un voisinage strict de ]X[_P dans ]Y[_P, dont la série de Taylor soit induite par un isomorphisme analytique p_2^*M ≅ p_1^*M sur un voisinage strict de ]X[_{P^2} dans ]Y[_{P^2}.” Statement (read from the page image).
- Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique p, (4.1), p. 25: “On dira que la connexion ∇ est convergente (pour X) si ε est induit par un isomorphisme analytique (nécessairement unique) sur ]X[_{P^2}” The convergent (non-overconvergent) analogue (read from the page image).

#### Lemma. Canonical isomorphisms between pullbacks along frame morphisms with the same reduction

*Node* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks`.

Let f, g : (X', Y', P') → (X, Y, P) be two morphisms of frames inducing the same morphisms X' → X and Y' → Y. For an overconvergent isocrystal (E, ε) on (X, Y, P), the pullback of ε along (f, g) : ]Y'[_{P'} → ]Y[_{P×P} defines an isomorphism χ_{f,g} : g^*E ≅ f^*E of overconvergent isocrystals; χ_{f,f} = id and χ_{f,g}∘χ_{g,h} = χ_{f,h}.

*Hypotheses.* (f, g) maps X' into the diagonal image of X, hence ]X'[_{P'} into ]X[_{P×P}, and strict neighbourhoods into strict neighbourhoods (RD.3/strict-neighbourhood).

*Proof outline.*

1. Pull back the stratification along (f, g); the cocycle identity for ε on ]Y[_{P³} pulled back along (f, g, h) gives the transitivity (standard crystal formalism; local analogue: Kedlaya overview Remark 4.1.9 for annuli).

*Acceptance.*

- For f = g the isomorphism is the identity; for two Frobenius lifts f, g of P̂^1 inducing t ↦ t^p mod π, χ_{f,g} on L_π is multiplication by exp π(g(t) − f(t)).

*Uses.* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/frame-pullback-functor`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/tube`.

*Sources.*

- Local monodromy of p-adic differential equations: an overview, Remark 4.1.9, p. 17: “Let f1 , f2 : A[a, 1) → A[b, 1) be two morphisms which induce the same map on Rint /mR . Then there is a natural isomorphism between the pullback functors f1∗ and f2∗ on Mconv , given by the Taylor series” Local analogue on annuli.
- Finiteness of rigid cohomology with coefficients, Definition 4.2.3, p. 26: “but in fact there are canonical equivalences (via pullbacks, and relying on the convergence condition) between the categories constructed using different P .” The role of the convergence condition in comparing pullbacks.

#### Theorem. Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals

*Node* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/independence-of-frame`.

(a) If (id_X, id_Y, u) : (X, Y, P') → (X, Y, P) is a morphism of frames with u smooth in a neighbourhood of X, then u^* : Isoc(X, Y, P/K) → Isoc(X, Y, P'/K) is an equivalence of categories. (b) For two frames (X, Y, P_1), (X, Y, P_2) with the same (X, Y), the projections from the diagonal frame (X, Y, P_1 ×_O P_2) are smooth near X, and the composite equivalences E_{12} := (p_2^*)^{-1}∘p_1^* are canonical: independent of choices up to unique isomorphism and satisfying E_{23}∘E_{12} ≅ E_{13}. Hence Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) := Isoc(X, Y, P/K) depends only on (X ⊂ Y) up to canonical equivalence, is local on Y, and is functorial in (X ⊂ Y). The same holds with Frobenius structures (RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal).

*Hypotheses.* P, P_i smooth near X; no hypothesis at the points of Z (Berthelot 2.3 remark). For Y without a global embedding into a formal scheme smooth near X, the category is defined by gluing along a Čech covering by frames (RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystals-of-a-variety).

*Proof outline.*

1. If u has a section s : P → P' over (X, Y), then s^* and u^* are quasi-inverse: s^*u^* = (us)^* = id and u^*s^* = (su)^* ≅ id^* by RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks (su and id_{P'} induce the same maps on X, Y).
2. In general, by RD.3/strong-fibration-theorem, locally on P there are strict neighbourhoods V' ≅ V × D(0,1^-)^n, so sections exist locally over strict neighbourhoods; the local quasi-inverses are compatible on overlaps by RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks and glue (descent of overconvergent isocrystals along admissible coverings of strict neighbourhoods, a stack property).
3. (b) The diagonal immersion Y → P_1 × P_2 is a closed immersion and the projections are smooth near X since P_i are; canonicity and the cocycle from RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks ('méthode du plongement diagonal', Berthelot 1.5).
4. PROOF SOURCE GAP for the gluing along the strong fibration: Berthelot 1986 states the result ('La catégorie ainsi obtenue ne dépend, à équivalence canonique près, que de X ⊂ Y'); the details are in his unpublished preprint and Le Stum's book (gaps).

*Acceptance.*

- Two embeddings of affine space: (A^n, P^n, P̂^n) and (A^n, P^n, P̂^n ×_O P̂^n) (diagonal) give canonically equivalent categories; see RD.3/affine-space-two-embeddings-acceptance for two different compactifications.
- For X smooth affine with lift A and two choices of presentation, the equivalence transports the (σ,∇)-module over A† ⊗ K realised in one presentation to the other by the Taylor isomorphism (Kedlaya Finiteness Remark 4.2.4: 'homotopy equivalences').

*Uses.* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/strong-fibration-theorem`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/frame-pullback-functor`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/frame`.

*Planet:* Independence of the frame.

*Sources.*

- Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique p, (4.2.1), p. 27: “La catégorie ainsi obtenue ne dépend, à équivalence canonique près, que de X ⊂ Y, est de nature locale sur Y, et est fonctorielle en (X,Y)/K.” Statement (read from the page image).
- Finiteness of rigid cohomology with coefficients, Remark 4.2.4, p. 26: “We reiterate that the equivalences of categories between different choices of P are homotopy equivalences on the level of de Rham complexes.” Nature of the equivalences.

#### Theorem. Independence of the compactification

*Node* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/independence-of-compactification`.

Let j : X ↪ Y and j' : X ↪ Y' be open immersions and v : Y' → Y a PROPER morphism with v∘j' = j and v^{-1}(X) = j'(X) (Kedlaya's formulation: f^{-1}(X) → X an isomorphism). Then v^* : Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) → Isoc†(X ⊂ Y'/K) is an equivalence of categories, compatible with Frobenius structures. Consequently, for a proper Y containing X as an open subscheme, Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) is independent of Y up to canonical equivalence (two compactifications are dominated by the closure of X in their product).

*Hypotheses.* Proper compactifications exist for separated finite type X by Nagata's theorem (request to SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0); for quasi-projective X one may take a projective closure.

*Proof outline.*

1. Choose frames Y ⊂ P and Y' ⊂ P' with a morphism u : P' → P lifting v (possible locally); after dévissage and base changes on P inducing an admissible covering of a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_P, reduce to the case where a section P → P' extends the section X → P' ×_P X given by j'; then replace Y' by the image of Y in P' and apply RD.3/independence-of-frame (Berthelot, sketch of the proof of Théorème 2 in 2.4, applied to isocrystals in 4.2.2).
2. PROOF SOURCE GAP: the full proof is Berthelot's unpublished Théorème 2.3.5 (preprint 96-03) or Le Stum, Theorem 7.1.8; Kedlaya's Notes Lemma 2.6 records both references (gaps).

*Acceptance.*

- X = A^2, Y = P^2 and Y' = the blow-up of P^2 at a point of the line at infinity: v^* is an equivalence although the boundaries Z = P^1 and Z' (two rational curves) differ.
- X = A^1, Y = P^1, Y' = the closure of the diagonal in P^1 × P^1 with v a projection: v is an isomorphism and v^* is the identity up to canonical isomorphism.

*Uses.* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/independence-of-frame`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/frame-pullback-functor`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/frame`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`.

*Sources.*

- Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique p, (4.2.2), p. 27: “On montre alors que le foncteur image inverse v^*, de la catégorie des cristaux sur X surconvergents le long de Z dans celle des cristaux sur X surconvergents le long de Z', est une équivalence de catégories.” Statement (read from the page image).
- Notes on isocrystals, Lemma 2.6, p. 3: “Then the pullback functor F-Isoc(X, Y ) → F-Isoc(X, Y ′ ) is an equivalence of categories.” Kedlaya's statement with Frobenius.
- Notes on isocrystals, Lemma 2.6 proof, p. 3: “The original but unpublished reference is [12, Théorème 2.3.5]. An alternate reference is [81, Theorem 7.1.8].” The proofs are in unavailable sources.

#### Theorem. Rigid-analytic Quillen-Suslin: finite projective modules over K⟨t_1..t_n⟩† are free

*Node* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/rigid-quillen-suslin`.

Every finite projective module over K⟨t_1, ..., t_n⟩† (overconvergent power series) is free; the same holds over O⟨t_1, ..., t_n⟩† when K is discretely valued. More precisely, for K complete with nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value and ρ = (ρ_i) with some power of each ρ_i in |K^×|, every finite projective module over the ring K⟨t⟩_ρ of series converging on the closed polydisc of polyradius ρ is free.

*Hypotheses.* The O-version requires K discretely valued, and Lemma 6.2 needs 'rank 1' in place of 'discrete' (published erratum by Davis-Schneider, Kedlaya's papers page).

*Proof outline.*

1. Weierstrass preparation over o⟨t⟩_ρ (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness, Lemma 6.1) and Noether-normalisation changes of variables T_j (Lemmas 6.2, 6.3) reduce unimodular rows over K⟨t⟩_ρ to rows over polynomial rings in one variable over K⟨t'⟩_{ρ'}; Lang's Algebra Theorem XXI.3.4 and induction give the unimodular extension property (Proposition 6.4).
2. Finite free resolutions by induction (Proposition 6.5), so finite projective modules are stably free and hence free (Proposition 6.6); pass to the direct limit over ρ > 1 (Theorem 6.7).

*Acceptance.*

- n = 1: for fixed ρ the ring K⟨t⟩_ρ is a principal ideal domain (Weierstrass preparation), so finite projective modules over it are free before passing to the limit over ρ > 1.

*Uses.* `AdicSpacesPartII:F1`, `mathlib:Module.Projective`, `mathlib:Module.Free`, `mathlib:IsPrincipalIdealRing`.

*Source.* Full faithfulness for overconvergent F-isocrystals, Theorem 6.7, p. 15: “Every finite projective module over Kht1 , . . . , tn i† or Oht1 , . . . , tn i† is free.” Statement (the extraction renders ⟨ ⟩ as h i).

#### Theorem. Overconvergent F-isocrystals on a smooth affine variety are (σ,∇)-modules over its dagger algebra

*Node* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/affine-smooth-description-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals`.

Let X be a smooth affine k-scheme, A a dagger algebra of MW-type with special fibre X (it exists and is unique up to non-canonical isomorphism), and σ a Frobenius lift on A. Choose a frame (X, Y, P) with P smooth over O_K near X. Then A ≅ colim_V Γ(V, O_V) over the strict neighbourhoods V of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P, and E ↦ M_E := colim_V Γ(V, E_V) is an equivalence between F-Isoc†(X/K) and the category of (σ,∇)-modules over A, compatible with tensor products, duals and pullbacks. For overconvergent isocrystals carrying a Frobenius structure, the convergence (Taylor) condition in the definition is automatic.

*Hypotheses.* X smooth affine over k; A of MW-type with A^int/πA^int ≅ O(X). The equivalence depends on σ only through the canonical change-of-Frobenius equivalence (RD.3/sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra, API changeOfFrobenius).

*Proof outline.*

1. Existence and uniqueness of A: van der Put, Theorem 2.4.4 (i), via Elkik's smooth lift and Artin approximation.
2. Identification of A with overconvergent functions: Berthelot (2.1) (the ring A† ⊗ K is the colimit of Γ(U_λ, O) over the affinoid neighbourhoods U_λ of the tube, which are strict neighbourhoods by (2.5) b)); with frames via RD.3/frame and RD.3/strict-neighbourhood.
3. Coherent sheaves on the affinoids U_λ correspond to finite Γ(U_λ)-modules (AdicSpacesPartII:R3), so a j†O-module locally free of finite rank gives a finite projective A-module M_E, and the connection gives ∇ on M_E.
4. The Frobenius structure F: σ^*E ≅ E gives the σ-semilinear F on M_E.
5. Essential surjectivity: for a (σ,∇)-module M over A, the Taylor isomorphism converges on a strict neighbourhood of the diagonal because of the Frobenius structure (Berthelot, preprint 96-03, Théorème 2.5.7, cited by Kedlaya, Remark 4.2.5); this step is recorded as a gap (source not public).
6. Full faithfulness: horizontal maps between overconvergent modules on V extend uniquely across the colimit.

*Acceptance.*

- X = A^1, A† = O⟨t⟩†: L_π corresponds to K⟨t⟩† with ∇(1) = π dt and Frobenius Φ(1) = exp π(t^p − t) for σ(t) = t^p.
- For X = A^1 the equivalence sends the constant object to (K⟨x⟩†, d, σ) and Berthelot's Dwork F-isocrystal L_π to (K⟨t⟩†, ∇1 = π dt, Φ(1) = exp π(t^p − t)) with K = ℚ_p(π), π^{p−1} = −p.

*Uses.* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergent-sections-of-affine-frame`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/rigid-quillen-suslin`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/frobenius-structure-forces-solvability`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/frame`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/tube`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3`.

*Sources.*

- Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique p, (4.2.2), pp. 27-28: “la catégorie des F-cristaux surconvergents sur X s'identifie alors à la catégorie des A†⊗K-modules projectifs de type fini M, munis :” Berthelot's description (read from the page image).
- Finiteness of rigid cohomology with coefficients, Remark 4.2.5, p. 26: “the main point is that in this setting, the convergence condition is an automatic consequence of the presence of a Frobenius structure [Be4, Théorème 2.5.7].” Automatic convergence.
- Finiteness of rigid cohomology with coefficients, Remark 4.2.5, p. 26: “For X smooth affine, the direct limit A of Γ(V, OV ) over all embeddings j :]X[→ V into a strict neighborhood is a dagger algebra of MW-type over K with special fibre X.” The dagger algebra as overconvergent functions.
- Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique p, (4.2.2), p. 27: “Lorsque X est affine et lisse d'algèbre A0 sur k, on peut la décrire en choisissant une 𝒱-algèbre lisse A de réduction A0 sur k, et de complétée faible A†, et un endomorphisme φ de A† relevant l'endomorphisme de Frobenius de A0” Berthelot's description of overconvergent F-crystals on smooth affines.
- The cohomology of Monsky and Washnitzer, Theorem 2.4.4, p. 37: “Let A/k be smooth and finitely generated. There exists a lift A of A. Moreover: (i) Every lift of A is R-isomorphic to A.” Existence and uniqueness of the dagger algebra.

#### Lemma. Extensions of (σ,∇)-modules over Γ_con with separated generic slopes split

*Node* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/splitting-of-slope-separated-extensions`.

(a) Let M be a σ-module over Γ^K_con[1/p] (K finite over k((t))) with all generic slopes positive. Then v ↦ Fv − v is injective on M ⊗ Γ^K_an,con, and if Fv − v ∈ M then v ∈ M. (b) If 0 → M_1 → M → M_2 → 0 is an exact sequence of (σ,∇)-modules over Γ_con with every generic slope of M_1 greater than every generic slope of M_2, the sequence splits over Γ_con[1/p].

*Hypotheses.* k is reduced to algebraically closed in the proof; the Frobenius σ = σ_0^f, q = p^f (the proof as printed uses p where q is meant, see sourceIssues).

*Proof outline.*

1. (a) Use de Jong's descending slope filtration (a basis with F triangular, diagonal λ_i of positive valuation, RD.1/generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent) and RD.1/cohomology-of-rank-one-frobenius-modules (a) coordinate by coordinate (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness, Lemma 3.2).
2. (b) The splitting is a solution X of −X + A X^σ D^{-1} = B. Over R_1 = Γ^L_an,con[log u] ⊗ O' it exists by the logarithmic form of local monodromy (RD.2/logarithmic-form-of-local-monodromy) and surjectivity of d/du on R_1 (RD.2/log-robba-ring-antiderivative). The matrices X form a σ-module with positive generic slopes, so by (a) the solution is unique and descends successively to Γ^L_an,con (no log terms), to Γ^L_an,con (no O'), to Γ^L_con[1/p] (by (a)), to Γ^K_con[1/p] (Galois invariance and uniqueness), and finally to Γ_con[1/p] (an eigenvector argument on a Frobenius-integral basis) (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness, Proposition 3.3).

*Acceptance.*

- For M_1 = Γ_con(1) (slope 1) and M_2 = Γ_con (slope 0) with trivial connections, every extension of (σ,∇)-modules splits over Γ_con[1/p].

*Uses.* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/logarithmic-form-of-local-monodromy`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/log-robba-ring-antiderivative`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/cohomology-of-rank-one-frobenius-modules`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings`.

*Sources.*

- Full faithfulness for overconvergent F-isocrystals, Proposition 3.3, p. 7: “Suppose there exists an exact se- quence 0 → M1 → M → M2 → 0 of (σ, ∇)-modules over Γcon such that the generic slopes of M1 are all greater than the generic slopes of M2 . Then the exact sequence splits over Γcon [ p1 ].” Part (b).
- Full faithfulness for overconvergent F-isocrystals, Lemma 3.2, p. 6: “whose generic slopes are all positive.” Hypothesis of part (a).

#### Lemma. de Jong's injectivity: Γ^alg_con ⊗_{Γ_con} Γ → Γ^alg is injective

*Node* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/de-jong-tensor-injectivity`.

For k algebraically closed (more generally for K admitting a valuation p-basis, SFR Proposition 2.2.21), the multiplication map Γ^alg_con ⊗_{Γ_con} Γ → Γ^alg is injective; moreover if x_1..x_n ∈ Γ are Γ_con-linearly independent and Σ x_i y_i ∈ Γ with y_i ∈ Γ^alg_con, then y_i ∈ Γ_con.

*Hypotheses.* Γ = Γ^{k((t))} (p-adic completion of R^int), Γ_con = R^int; Γ^alg, Γ^alg_con as in RD.0/extended-robba-ring.

*Proof outline.*

1. Embed into the maximal immediate extension (Hahn-Kaplansky generalised power series) and expand every element uniquely as Σ_{α∈[0,1)} x_α w^α with x_α ∈ Γ and w the Teichmüller lift of t; overconvergent elements have overconvergent coefficients x_α; conclude by the uniqueness of the expansion and the minimal-counterexample argument (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness, Proposition 4.1, after de Jong Proposition 8.1). Alternatively: Galois invariance plus a Γ-linear section f : Γ^perf → Γ preserving overconvergence (SFR Lemma 2.2.19, Proposition 2.2.21).

*Acceptance.*

- For x = 1 the statement says Γ ∩ Γ^alg_con = Γ_con inside Γ^alg (compare arXiv:math/0110124 Corollary 3.8).

*Uses.* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/extended-robba-ring`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/analytic-ring`, `mathlib:HahnSeries`.

*Sources.*

- Full faithfulness for overconvergent F-isocrystals, Proposition 4.1, p. 9: “For k algebraically closed, the multiplication map” Statement (continues: Γ^alg_con ⊗_{Γ_con} Γ → Γ^alg is injective).
- Slope filtrations revisited, Proposition 2.2.21(c), p. 11: “The map µ is injective.” SFR generalisation (valuation p-basis).

#### Lemma. Maps to Γ with Frobenius eigenvalue p^m detect a rank one slope-ℓ submodule

*Node* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/de-jong-rank-one-image`.

Let M be a nonzero σ-module over Γ_con (K = k((t)), k algebraically closed) and φ : M → Γ an injective Γ_con-linear map with φ(Fv) = p^m φ(v)^σ for all v and some integer m ≥ 0. Then the largest generic slope of M is m, with multiplicity 1, and φ^{-1}(Γ_con) is a σ-submodule of M of rank 1 and slope m.

*Hypotheses.* Slopes here are p-adic valuations of eigenvalues, as in the source (an eigenvector with F v = λ v has slope v_p(λ)); σ = σ_0^f is a q-power Frobenius lift, q = p^f, and the Tate twist by ℓ multiplies F by q^ℓ, so the lemma is applied with m = fℓ (see RD.3/local-full-faithfulness).

*Proof outline.*

1. φ extends injectively to M ⊗ Γ^alg_con by RD.3/de-jong-tensor-injectivity; eigenvectors of maximal slope s from the descending generic filtration (RD.1/generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent) satisfy λφ(v) = p^m φ(v)^σ, forcing s = v_p(λ) = m, and then φ(v) lies in the σ-fixed constants, forcing multiplicity 1; nonemptiness of φ^{-1}(Γ_con) via the generalised power series expansion (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness, Lemma 4.2, after de Jong Corollary 8.2).

*Acceptance.*

- M = Γ_con with F(1) = p^m (a rank one σ-module of slope m, for σ fixing p) and φ the inclusion into Γ: φ^{-1}(Γ_con) = M.

*Uses.* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/de-jong-tensor-injectivity`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent`.

*Source.* Full faithfulness for overconvergent F-isocrystals, Lemma 4.2, p. 10: “Then the largest generic slope of M is equal to ℓ, occurring with multiplicity 1. Moreover, φ−1 (Γcon ) is a σ-submodule of M of dimension 1 with slope ℓ.” Statement.

#### Theorem. Local full faithfulness: morphisms of (σ,∇)-modules over Γ_con are determined over Γ

*Node* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/local-full-faithfulness`.

Let M_1, M_2 be (σ,∇)-modules over Γ_con = R^int (K = k((t))) and f : M_1 ⊗ Γ → M_2 ⊗ Γ a morphism of (σ,∇)-modules over Γ. Then f is induced by a (unique) morphism g : M_1 → M_2 over Γ_con. Equivalently, F-Isoc†(k((t))) → F-Isoc(k((t))) is fully faithful (Tsuzuki's Conjecture 2.3.2 in [T2]).

*Hypotheses.* The local model of the global theorem (Kedlaya, Notes Remark 5.5).

*Proof outline.*

1. Reduce to a Γ_con-linear φ : M = M_1^∨(ℓ) ⊗ M_2 → Γ (ℓ large, so that the twist is defined over Γ_con) with φ(Fv) = q^ℓ φ(v)^σ = p^{fℓ} φ(v)^σ and φ(∇v) = u d/du φ(v), and k algebraically closed; show φ(M) ⊆ Γ_con (the printed proof writes p^ℓ φ(v) for q^ℓ φ(v)^σ, see sourceIssues).
2. Replace M by M/ker φ; by RD.3/de-jong-rank-one-image with m = fℓ, P = ψ^{-1}(Γ_con) is of rank one and of slope fℓ, strictly greater than all other generic slopes; P is ∇-stable because du^σ/du is divisible by π (u^σ ≡ u^q mod π), which makes the two sides of the Frobenius equation for ψ(∇v) have different valuations unless ∇v = 0.
3. 0 → P → M/N → (M/N)/P → 0 splits by RD.3/splitting-of-slope-separated-extensions; the complement Q must vanish by RD.3/de-jong-rank-one-image again; hence φ(M) = ψ(P) ⊆ Γ_con (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness, Theorem 5.1).

*Acceptance.*

- For M_1 = M_2 = Γ_con with the trivial (σ,∇)-structure, a morphism over Γ is multiplication by an element c of Γ with c^σ = c and dc = 0, and such c already lie in the constants of Γ_con (the fixed field of σ on the coefficient ring), so the statement holds trivially in rank one with trivial structure.

*Uses.* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/de-jong-rank-one-image`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/splitting-of-slope-separated-extensions`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/frobenius-module`.

*Source.* Full faithfulness for overconvergent F-isocrystals, Theorem 5.1, p. 11: “Let M1 and M2 be (σ, ∇)-modules over Γcon , and let f : M1 ⊗Γcon Γ → M2 ⊗Γcon Γ be a morphism of (σ, ∇)-modules over Γ. Then there exists a morphism g : M1 → M2 that induces f .” Statement.

#### Theorem. Open dense affines finite étale over affine space in positive characteristic

*Node* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/etale-cover-of-affine-space`.

Let k be a field of characteristic p > 0 and X a separated, geometrically reduced k-scheme of finite type and pure dimension n, and x a smooth (geometric) point of X. Then X contains an open dense affine subscheme U containing x with a finite étale morphism U → A^n_k. (Kedlaya's Proposition 9.1.2 says 'of dimension n'; purity is needed, see sourceIssues.)

*Hypotheses.* Pure dimension n (a finite étale map to A^n has all components of dimension n and U must meet every component). Geometrically reduced (each component generically smooth).

*Proof outline.*

1. Kedlaya, More étale covers, Theorem 1: a geometrically reduced projective X of pure dimension n admits a finite morphism to P^n induced by sections of a power of an ample line bundle, étale away from the hyperplane H at infinity, sending a chosen divisor D into H and chosen smooth points outside H; the proof is a Noether normalisation by sections vanishing on D (Lemmas 3–6, with care for finite k), with unramifiedness at the chosen points.
2. Theorem 2 there deduces the statement for separated finite-type X: compactify, apply Theorem 1 with D containing the boundary and the non-smooth locus, and restrict to the preimage of A^n = P^n \ H.

*Acceptance.*

- For X = A^n itself, U = A^n with the identity.
- X = A^1: U = A^1 with the identity. X = G_m: x ↦ x + x^{-1}… is not étale in characteristic 2; an Artin–Schreier-type map exists by the theorem (the case n = 1 is attributed to Abhyankar).

*Uses.* `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType`.

*Sources.*

- Full faithfulness for overconvergent F-isocrystals, Lemma 7.1, p. 16: “Then there exists an open dense subset U of X, containing x and defined over k, such that U admits a finite étale map over k to affine n-space.” Statement.
- Finiteness of rigid cohomology with coefficients, Proposition 9.1.2, p. 61: “Let X be a separated, geometrically reduced, finite type k-scheme of dimension n, for k a field of characteristic p > 0, and let x be a smooth geometric point of X. Then X contains an open dense affine subscheme containing x and admitting a finite étale morphism to affine n-space.” Kedlaya's statement.
- More étale covers of affine spaces in positive characteristic, Theorem 2, p. 2: “Let X be a separated scheme of finite type over k (still of characteristic p > 0) of pure dimension n, let x be a smooth point of X, and let D1 , . . . , Dm be irreducible divisors of X intersecting transversely at x.” The source theorem, with pure dimension.
- More étale covers of affine spaces in positive characteristic, Section 1, p. 1: “(The case n = 1 seems to have become a folk theorem, but we believe it is originally due to Abhyankar.)” Attribution.

#### Theorem. Kedlaya's full faithfulness theorem: overconvergent F-isocrystals embed fully faithfully into convergent ones

*Node* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent`.

Let k be a field of characteristic p, K as in the setting, X a SMOOTH separated k-scheme of finite type and a ≥ 1. Then the restriction functor j^* : F^a-Isoc†(X/K) → F^a-Isoc(X/K) (RD.3/restriction-to-convergent) is fully faithful. More generally (de Jong, Kedlaya, Shiho; Kedlaya Notes Theorem 5.3), for X ⊆ Y and U ⊆ X open dense, U ⊆ W ⊆ Y open, F-Isoc(X, Y) → F-Isoc(U, W) is fully faithful. Proven range: WITH Frobenius structures; for isocrystals without Frobenius the analogue for F-Isoc† → F-Isoc fails (Kedlaya Notes Remark 5.6, citing Abe), and the full faithfulness is not an essential surjectivity (the image is a proper subcategory).

*Hypotheses.* Unit-root case earlier: Tsuzuki (X with smooth compactification) and Étesse (general X). The theorem uses the p-adic local monodromy theorem in logarithmic form (RD.2) through RD.3/splitting-of-slope-separated-extensions.

*Proof outline.*

1. Reduce to H^0: Hom(E_1, E_2) = H^0_F(X, E_1^∨ ⊗ E_2) (Frobenius-fixed horizontal sections) in both categories, so it suffices that H^0_F has the same rank (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness §7).
2. The question is local on X; by RD.3/etale-cover-of-affine-space cover X by opens U finite étale over A^n, and by RD.3/finite-etale-pushforward-of-isocrystals (H^0_F(X, E) = H^0_F(A^n, f_*E)) reduce to X = A^n.
3. On A^n (with a = f, q = p^a), E is a (σ,∇)-module M over R = O⟨x_1..x_n⟩†[1/p]; a twist M(ℓ) is defined over R and free by RD.3/rigid-quillen-suslin; a Frobenius-invariant horizontal v over the p-adic completion R^∧ lies in M(ℓ) ⊗ R_i for each i by RD.3/local-full-faithfulness applied in the variable x_i (R_i = S_i⟨x_i⟩†), and ∩_i R_i = R gives v ∈ M(ℓ) (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness §7).

*Acceptance.*

- Unit-root case: F-Isoc† unit-root objects ↔ potentially unramified p-adic local systems ⊂ all p-adic local systems ↔ unit-root convergent objects (Katz-Crew, Tsuzuki; Notes Theorems 3.7, 3.9): the embedding is fully faithful but not essentially surjective.
- On the ordinary locus U of X(N), the unit-root line subobject of E|_U exists convergently but not overconvergently (Notes Example 4.6, Remark 5.12): full faithfulness does not give extension of subobjects.

*Uses.* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/etale-cover-of-affine-space`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/finite-etale-pushforward-of-isocrystals`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/rigid-quillen-suslin`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/local-full-faithfulness`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/restriction-to-convergent`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.Full`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.Faithful`.

*Planet:* Full faithfulness theorem.

*Sources.*

- Full faithfulness for overconvergent F-isocrystals, Theorem 1.1, p. 2: “Theorem 1.1. The forgetful functor j ∗ : F a -Isoc† (X/K) → F a -Isoc(X/K) is fully faithful.” Statement (X smooth separated of finite type).
- Notes on isocrystals, Theorem 5.3, p. 12: “The restriction functor F-Isoc(X, Y ) → F-Isoc(U, W ) is fully faithful.” General form (de Jong, Kedlaya, Shiho).
- Notes on isocrystals, Remark 5.6, p. 13: “but the analogue of full faithfulness for F-Isoc† (X) to F-Isoc(X) fails (see [1]).” Failure without Frobenius (Abe).

#### Application. Acceptance: the proven range of full faithfulness

*Node* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/full-faithfulness-requires-frobenius`.

The restriction functor from overconvergent to convergent isocrystals is fully faithful WITH Frobenius structures (RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent), but the analogous statement for isocrystals WITHOUT Frobenius structure fails (Kedlaya Notes Remark 5.6, citing Abe), the failure being related to p-adic Liouville numbers; whereas the analogue of full faithfulness of F-Isoc†(X) → F-Isoc†(U) (U ⊆ X dense open) does hold without Frobenius. Any formal statement of full faithfulness in this roadmap therefore carries the Frobenius hypothesis.

*Hypotheses.* Recorded as an acceptance boundary, not as a theorem proved here; Abe's counterexample (IMRN 2011) is not in the public source set.

*Proof outline.*

1. Cite Kedlaya Notes Remark 5.6; the positive direction is RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent; the Liouville phenomenon is illustrated by Crew's criterion: the connection ∇_C = d + C dx/x on the Robba ring is strict iff the eigenvalues of C are not p-adic Liouville numbers (Crew Proposition 6.10).

*Acceptance.*

- Test: the statement node RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent has 'Frobenius structure' among its hypotheses (checked in this packet).

*Uses.* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent`.

*Sources.*

- Notes on isocrystals, Remark 5.6, p. 13: “The latter is related to known pathologies in the theory of p-adic differential equations re- lated to p-adic Liouville numbers” Liouville numbers.
- Full faithfulness for overconvergent F-isocrystals, Introduction, p. 2: “Tsuzuki further conjectures that the same statement holds for isocrystals without Frobenius structure, but the methods of this paper do not extend to that case.” The Frobenius-free question (later answered negatively, per Kedlaya Notes Remark 5.6).
- Finiteness theorems for the cohomology of an overconvergent isocrystal on a curve, Proposition 6.10, p. 740: “The connection ∇_C is strict if and only if the eigenvalues of C are not p-adic Liouville numbers.” Crew's criterion (read from the scan; OCR renders ∇ as V).

#### Application. Acceptance: the frames A^n ⊂ P^n and A^n ⊂ (P^1)^n give equivalent categories

*Node* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/affine-space-two-embeddings-acceptance`.

Let X = A^n_k with the two compactifications Y_1 = P^n_k and Y_2 = (P^1_k)^n and frames (X, Y_1, P̂^n_O), (X, Y_2, (P̂^1_O)^n). (a) In both frames the tube ]X[ is the closed unit polydisc {|t_i| ≤ 1}, and the polydiscs V_λ = {|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1} for all i} (λ < 1, λ → 1) form a cofinal family of strict neighbourhoods, so Γ(]Y_i[, j†O) = K⟨t_1, ..., t_n⟩† in both cases. (b) The equivalence Isoc†(A^n ⊂ P^n/K) ≃ Isoc†(A^n ⊂ (P^1)^n/K) of RD.3/independence-of-compactification is realised through the closure Y_3 of the diagonal of A^n in P^n × (P^1)^n, whose projections to Y_1 and Y_2 are proper and are isomorphisms over A^n, with the frame (X, Y_3, P̂^n × (P̂^1)^n) mapping to both frames; on the pullback of the Dwork isocrystal along the first coordinate it sends (K⟨t_1..t_n⟩†, ∇(1) = π dt_1) to itself.

*Hypotheses.* n ≥ 1; for n = 1 the two compactifications coincide and the statement is the identity.

*Proof outline.*

1. (a) In P^n with homogeneous coordinates x_0..x_n and Z = {x_0 = 0}: ]Z[_λ = {|x_0| < λ max_i |x_i|}, whose complement is {|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1}}, t_i = x_i/x_0 (Berthelot 2.1: 'un exercice facile sur les coordonnées projectives'). In (P^1)^n, Z = ∪_i {t_i = ∞} is cut out near a boundary point by the product of the coordinates s_i = 1/t_i with |t_i| ≥ 1, so the complement W_λ of ]Z[_λ is {|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1} for all i, and |Π_{i∈I} t_i| ≤ λ^{-1} for the set I of indices with |t_i| ≥ 1}; hence W_λ ⊆ V_λ ⊆ W_{λ^n}, and the two families are cofinal. Global sections: RD.3/overconvergent-sections-of-affine-frame.
2. (b) The graph closure Y_3 ⊆ Y_1 × Y_2 contains X as an open subscheme with v_i^{-1}(X) = X for both projections v_i (both are isomorphisms over A^n), so RD.3/independence-of-compactification applies to v_1 and v_2; the diagonal frame is smooth over O (RD.3/independence-of-frame (b)).
3. Computation: under both identifications the pullback of the Dwork isocrystal along the first coordinate t_1 is the free rank one K⟨t_1..t_n⟩†-module with ∇(1) = π dt_1, and its Taylor isomorphism exp π(t'_1 − t_1) is analytic on the strict neighbourhood {|t_1 − t'_1| < 1} of the diagonal tube in either frame (Berthelot 4.2.3 b for n = 1).

*Acceptance.*

- Test: strict neighbourhoods agree: for λ < 1 the complement of ]Z_1[_λ in (P^n)^an is exactly the polydisc V_λ = {|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1}}, and the complement W_λ of ]Z_2[_λ in ((P^1)^n)^an satisfies W_λ ⊆ V_λ ⊆ W_{λ^n} (for n = 2 and |t_1|, |t_2| ≥ 1, W_λ is {|t_1 t_2| ≤ λ^{-1}}, strictly smaller than V_λ).
- Test: global sections of j†O in both frames equal K⟨t_1..t_n⟩† (the union over λ of the Tate algebras of the polydiscs of radius λ^{-1}).

*Uses.* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/independence-of-frame`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/independence-of-compactification`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergent-sections-of-affine-frame`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/frame`.

*Sources.*

- Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique p, (2.1), p. 16: “Un exercice facile sur les coordonnées projectives montre que, pour λ < 1, on a encore” The tube of the divisor at infinity of P^n with radius λ (read from the page image).
- Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique p, (4.2.2), p. 27: “la catégorie des cristaux sur X surconvergents le long de X̄-X ne dépend donc, à équivalence canonique près, que de X, et est par définition la catégorie des cristaux surconvergents sur X/K.” Independence of the compactification (read from the page image).

#### Application. Acceptance: on punctured curves the boundary behaviour separates overconvergent from convergent

*Node* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/punctured-curve-boundary-acceptance`.

(a) On X = A^1_{F_p} = P^1 − {∞} over K = Q_p(π), π^{p−1} = −p, the Dwork isocrystal L_π (∇(1) = π dt) is overconvergent: its Taylor isomorphism exp π(t' − t) is analytic on |t − t'| < 1, a strict neighbourhood of the diagonal tube, and its Frobenius exp π(t^p − t) converges on |t| < p^{(p−1)/p²}; it has H^*_rig(X/K, L_π) = H^*_c(X/K, L_π) = 0, and its local monodromy at ∞ is trivialised by an Artin-Schreier extension (RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example). (b) Convergence alone is insufficient: the naive (convergent) de Rham cohomology of A^n is that of the closed polydisc and is infinite-dimensional over K; the convergent F-isocrystal E on A^1 given by ∇e_1 = 0, ∇e_2 = (Σ_{k≥0} p^k t^{p^k − 1} dt) e_1, F(σ^*e_1) = e_1, F(σ^*e_2) = e_2 − t e_1 (σ(t) = t^p) is an extension of the constant object by itself which is not overconvergent; and on the ordinary locus U = X(N) − Z of the modular curve (a curve punctured at the supersingular points) the unit-root subobject of the crystalline H^1 of the universal elliptic curve exists as a convergent but not as an overconvergent F-isocrystal.

*Hypotheses.* p odd in the Dwork computations; K = Q_p(π) with σ_K = id and q = p. The extension E of (b) is the explicit form of Kedlaya's Notes Remark 5.13, whose printed 'X = A^1_K' should read A^1_k (sourceIssues).

*Proof outline.*

1. (a) Overconvergence of L_π: Berthelot 4.2.3 b)-c); the Frobenius series: PARI/GP check that v_p of the n-th coefficient of exp π(t − t^p) is at least n(p−1)/p² for n ≤ 200 and p = 3, 5, 7 (checks/dwork.out), in agreement with Dwork's estimate. Vanishing of rigid cohomology: Berthelot's exercise at the end of 4.2.4 (to be carried out in RD.4).
2. (b1) Naive cohomology: H^1_dR of the closed disc K⟨t⟩ is infinite-dimensional because an antiderivative of Σ a_n t^n dt lies in K⟨t⟩ only if a_n/(n+1) → 0 (Berthelot 1.5, Remarque after Proposition 2); the form ω below is Part A's example RD.0/completion-versus-overconvergence (b).
3. (b2) E is a convergent F-isocrystal: ω = Σ p^k t^{p^k−1} dt lies in K⟨t⟩dt, its antiderivative G = Σ t^{p^k} converges on every open disc of radius 1 (convergence of the connection), and σ^*ω − ω = d(G(t^p) − G(t)) = −dt, which is the compatibility of ∇ with F(σ^*e_2) = e_2 − t e_1 (PARI/GP check of σ^*ω − ω = −dt through degree p^6, checks/algebra.out). E is not overconvergent: if E ≅ j^*E', then by RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent the sequence comes from an extension of O^† by O^† in F-Isoc†(A^1), so ω − dg ∈ K⟨t⟩†dt for some g ∈ K⟨t⟩; since K⟨t⟩† is stable under antiderivatives, G − g ∈ K⟨t⟩†, hence G ∈ K⟨t⟩, contradicting that the coefficients of G do not tend to 0.
4. (b3) The unit-root subobject on the ordinary locus: Kedlaya Notes Example 4.6 and Remark 5.12 (a supersingular elliptic curve has no distinguished line in its rigid cohomology).

*Acceptance.*

- Test: exp π(t − t^p) has coefficient valuations ≥ n(p−1)/p² (numerically checked), while exp(πt) has coefficient valuations exactly s_p(n)/(p−1) (radius exactly 1, checked for n ≤ 200, p = 3, 5): the Frobenius structure is overconvergent although the horizontal section is not.
- Test: σ^*ω − ω = −dt for ω = Σ p^k t^{p^k−1} dt (checked for p = 3, 5 through degree p^6 up to the truncated top term).

*Uses.* `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/restriction-to-convergent`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/affine-smooth-description-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/completion-versus-overconvergence`.

*Sources.*

- Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique p, (4.2.3) b), p. 29: “La fonction expπ(t'-t) est analytique (rigide) sur l'ouvert admissible U de A^{2 an}_K défini par |t-t'| < 1 ; on vérifie immédiatement que U est un voisinage strict de ]X[ dans ]X̄[.” Overconvergence of the Dwork Taylor isomorphism (read from the page image).
- Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique p, Exercice after (4.2.4), p. 29: “Exercice : Vérifier que, si K = Q_p(π) et X = A^1_{F_p}, on a H*_rig(X/K, L_π) = H*_c(X/K, L_π) = 0.” Vanishing of the Dwork cohomology (read from the page image).
- Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique p, (1.5), Remarque after Proposition 2, p. 15: “la cohomologie naïve de l'espace affine A^n sur k est la cohomologie de De Rham du polydisque fermé D(0,1^+)^n, qui n'est pas de dimension finie sur K.” Convergence is insufficient (read from the page image).
- Notes on isocrystals, Remark 5.13, p. 14: “this already fails in case X = A1K and E1 , E2 are both the constant object in” Extensions of constant objects need not be overconvergent.
- Notes on isocrystals, Example 4.6, p. 9: “the restriction of E to F-Isoc(U) admits a rank 1 subobject which is unit-root. However, no such subobject exists in F-Isoc† (U); see Remark 5.12.” Unit-root subobject on the ordinary locus.
